main_text.p: Astrin-gentia se-cunda mensa sumta cur aluũ subdu-cant?ctionem interturbant : ficut astringendi vi prædita, vt cotonea, secunda mensa sumta, subducendæ aluo conueniunt, comprimen-do enim ac astringendo os ventriculi robo-rant, quo fit vt citius aluus deiiciat. Primam igitur mensam subibunt, cerafa, pruna, perfi-ca, mora, & id genus alia fugacia & præcocia, quorum videl. gratia statim ttansuolat, mu-stea[?] item & mellita plæraq;. Videant igitur, qui secundas mensas cerafis, prunis ac perfi-cis exornant, qui tamen mos adeo in lautioribus mensis inualuit, principumque aulis, vt gulæ ac palato detractum putent, si non NB.apposita fuerint. Eadem ratione valetudinem non parum infirmant, qui primis mensis vescuntur solidis cibis & duris, vt sunt carnes infumatæ indurataque, & quæ vel de prandio vel cœna sublatæ referuataque sequenti die iterum apponuntur. Sanitatis enim tuendæ præceptum non postremum est, calida, quatenus calida, frigidis, mollia duris, humida ficcis sunt præmittenda. Sic poma ante cotonea, hæc vero ante castaneas esitasse conuenit. Et hæc ἐν πρώτῳ[?] & proemii loco præmonuisse placuit.

Fructus igitur salubriores adq; rem ci-bariam pertinentes sunt poma, pyra, cerafa, mora, fraga, pruna, persica, melones, pepones, cucumeres, cotonea, mespila, sorba, ca-staneæ, nux juglans, auellana, amygdalæ, pi-

page.notes: The left-margin keyword note is printed in the margin in several hyphenated lines ("eAstrin-", "gentia se-", "cunda", "mensa", "sumta", "cur aluũ", "subdu-", "cant.?"); the leading "e" before "Astrin" is doubtful and may be a stray mark. The word after "mu-" at the end of a line ("ftea") is doubtful. The Greek phrase after "hæc" is doubtful. "ttansuolat" is printed as shown. The running head is set in small capitals and is given as "De Vita". The page number is read as 278. The catchword "sta-" is at the lower right.
